start_here: Say to your AI: "Run my workflow check-a-formula now." It reads that workflow's row from where you keep your workflows, runs tool:run-a-workflow with the row's definition, and tells you which step it reached: here the step that asks tool:evaluate-a-formula, which the engine starts at once and whose answer runs the workflow on to its end.
no_lists_because: It keeps nothing and names no list: the definition is handed in by whatever starts the run, from the person's own workflow rows, and every answer travels back in the fact that runs it again.
instructions: 1. Keep the workflow as a row of your own (its definition: id, name, kind workflow, is_active, version, steps, edges).
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:run-a-workflow and input {definition, and the workflow's own input fields}.
3. Read result.status and result.waiting: each step that names a tool is started for you, and each other step waits for whoever it names, with told_as saying how its answer comes back.

4. To have it run by itself, switch on its wakes: a-workflow-was-chosen (a router tells the chosen row), a-step-was-answered (answers come back), a-step-is-waiting (your switch input carries the definition that gives a waiting step to whoever it names, such as a task row) and a-row-changed (your switch input carries the definition to run on every change).

worked_examples.title: A one-step workflow starts the formula tool and waits for its answer
